content:
Starting today, WhatsApp Web users can directly view, review, and annotate PDF files within chats. Details below.

Adobe Acrobat is now available on WhatsApp Web

Previously, when users received a PDF file on WhatsApp, they had to download it before opening it, and the platform had no built-in review or annotation tools.

Adobe announced today that its Acrobat PDF tools have been directly integrated into WhatsApp Web and the Windows version of the WhatsApp app, allowing users to open, review, and annotate documents without needing to download files or leave the conversation.

Adobe stated that, in addition to standard PDF files, the integration also supports password-protected documents, and files shared in chats are also protected by WhatsApp's end-to-end encryption, "meaning that only members of the conversation can read the content."

Adobe pointed out that this integration reflects two trends: on one hand, users are increasingly using WhatsApp on larger screens to handle tasks such as reviewing contracts, invoices, forms, and assignments; on the other hand, it is part of Adobe's broader strategy to bring Acrobat's PDF tools to the platforms where users do their daily work, such as Chrome, Microsoft 365 and Copilot, ChatGPT, Workday, and others.
